headline: Biomolecular Modeling Reaches RNA Binding, Pseudoknot Design and AlphaFold3 Evaluation
label: Biomolecular Structure Modeling Foundations
summary: AlphaFold3 benchmarks and RNA-targeted methods now test structure prediction on non-canonical and complex biomolecular targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the extension of biomolecular structure modeling beyond single-chain proteins to RNA and immune receptor targets. Ribo-LENS applies geometric deep learning with adaptive 2.5D base-pairing subgraph search to detect RNA small-molecule binding sites and is reported to outperform AlphaFold3 and Chai-1. PKProbDesign addresses RNA inverse folding for pseudoknotted targets by optimizing thermodynamic folding probability and outperforms DesiRNA. A separate preprint evaluates AlphaFold3 across ubiquitinated proteins, TCR-epitope, antibody-antigen, protein-RNA and protein-lipid tasks, reporting uneven performance and training-data dependence. A JCIM review proposes evaluation standards for machine learning models of drug-RNA interactions and benchmarks them. The new element is explicit treatment of RNA structural motifs and complex interfaces, paired with critical assessment of how well existing predictors transfer across application areas.
